claude.sample_unit: individuals undergoing LDCT lung cancer screening
models_evaluated: commercial AI computer-aided detection tool for lung nodules

links.outcome: Recall rate, specificity, sensitivity and time for radiologists with vs without AI assistance
links.effect: AI assistant: recall 30.3% vs 22.1% (p<.001), specificity 81.1% vs 88.8%, sensitivity 64.8% vs 64.2% (p=.86), time 161 vs 164 s (p=.48).
links.quote: Compared with interpretation without AI (recall rate, 22.1%; per-nodule sensitivity, 64.2%; per-examination specificity, 88.8%; mean interpretation time, 164 seconds), AI as an assistant showed higher recall rate (30.3%; p < .001), lower per-examination specificity (81.1%), and no significant change in per-nodule sensitivity (64.8%; p = .86) or mean interpretation time (161 seconds; p = .48)

links.outcome: Reader performance with AI assistance in workflow versus without AI
links.effect: AI assistance raised recall rate to 30.3% from 22.1% and lowered specificity to 81.1% from 88.8%, with no sensitivity gain (64.8% vs 64.2%).
links.quote: Compared with interpretation without AI (recall rate, 22.1%; per-nodule sensitivity, 64.2%; per-examination specificity, 88.8%; mean interpretation time, 164 seconds), AI as an assistant showed higher recall rate (30.3%; p < .001), lower per-examination specificity (81.1%), and no significant change in per-nodule sensitivity (64.8%; p = .86) or mean interpretation time (161 seconds; p = .48)

links.outcome: Outcomes when radiologists interpret only AI-positive exams versus all exams
links.effect: AI prescreener (radiologists read only AI-positive exams): recall 20.8% (p=.02), time 143 s (p=.001), specificity 90.3% (p=.04), sensitivity 62.9% (p=.16, not significant).
links.quote: AI as a prescreener showed lower recall rate (20.8%; p = .02) and mean interpretation time (143 seconds; p = .001), higher per-examination specificity (90.3%; p = .04), and no significant difference in per-nodule sensitivity (62.9%; p = .16)

links.outcome: Net benefit and workload of AI utilization scenarios in LDCT screening
links.effect: Only AI as prescreener had higher net benefit than interpretation without AI; assistant had least net benefit.
links.quote: Among scenarios, only AI as a prescreener demonstrated higher net benefit than interpretation without AI; AI as an assistant had the least net benefit.

unlisted_practices: Using AI as a prescreener to triage which LDCT screening exams require radiologist interpretation
Using AI as a backup to prompt radiologist reinterpretation of exams with possibly missed findings

links.effect: Only prescreener had higher net benefit than no AI; assistant had least net benefit. Prescreener sensitivity 62.9% vs 64.2%, time 143 vs 164 seconds.
links.quote: Among scenarios, only AI as a prescreener demonstrated higher net benefit than interpretation without AI; AI as an assistant had the least net benefit.

links.effect: Prescreener: per-nodule sensitivity 62.9% vs 64.2% (p = .16); specificity 90.3% vs 88.8% (p = .04); time 143 vs 164 seconds.
links.quote: An approach whereby radiologists only interpret LDCT examinations with a positive AI result can reduce radiologists' workload while preserving sensitivity.

links.outcome: diagnostic outcomes, reading time, and net benefit across AI scenarios
links.effect: AI prescreener had higher specificity (90.3% vs 88.8%, p=.04), lower reading time (143 vs 164s, p=.001), preserved sensitivity (62.9% vs 64.2%, p=.16), and highest net benefit; assistant reading all cases had least net benefit.
links.quote: Compared with interpretation without AI (recall rate, 22.1%; per-nodule sensitivity, 64.2%; per-examination specificity, 88.8%; mean interpretation time, 164 seconds), AI as an assistant showed higher recall rate (30.3%; p < .001), lower per-examination specificity (81.1%), and no significant change in per-nodule sensitivity (64.8%; p = .86) or mean interpretation time (161 seconds; p = .48); AI as a prescreener showed lower recall rate (20.8%; p = .02) and mean interpretation time (143 seconds; p = .001), higher per-examination specificity (90.3%; p = .04), and no significant difference in per-nodule sensitivity (62.9%; p = .16); and AI as a backup showed increased recall rate (33.6%; p < .001), per-examination sensitivity (66.4%; p < .001), and mean interpretation time (225 seconds; p = .001), with lower per-examination specificity (79.9%; p < .001).

unlisted_practices: AI as backup reader (prompting reinterpretation when AI suggests missed finding)
